status_detail: Approved, not started: the state register (last modified 2026-10-06) says 'The demonstration period has not started yet.'
what_is_allowed: August AI may deploy a refill platform for routine refills of existing, provider-prescribed medications for patients with an established treatment plan. No new prescriptions, dose changes or substitutions. Each medication cohort moves separately through Phase 1 (first 250 refills reviewed by a Utah provider before release), Phase 2 (AI authorizes next 1,000, each reviewed retrospectively), Phase 3 (sampled oversight).
drug_scope: Pre-approved formulary of non-controlled maintenance medications; excludes controlled substances, narcotics, stimulants, injectables, antibiotics and any acute/short-term medication.
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: 'A Utah-licensed health care provider remains the accountable named prescriber for each refill and retains override authority at all times.'
start_date: Signed 2026-10-01/02; commencement when product launches and Office is notified (not started per register)
notes: Register: a Utah-licensed provider reviews the first 250 refills before they reach the patient and each of the next 1,000 afterward; then spot checks of at least 5% per medication class; no more than three AI refills in a row per medication at the start. Checked 2026-11-12.
short: August AI: routine refills
review_now: When it starts: a provider reviews the first 250 refills before they reach the patient.
next: Then 1,000 reviewed after the fact, then spot checks of at least 5% per medication class.

status_detail: Active on the state register; Phase 1 (a licensed practitioner authorizes every renewal). The listed term ended 2026-10-24 and no extension, suspension or end had been published as of 2026-11-12.
what_is_allowed: Doctronic's AI may authorize renewal of a Utah resident's verified existing prescription (30/60/90-day) and send it to a Utah pharmacist, under a regulatory mitigation agreement that suspends unlicensed-practice enforcement. No new prescriptions, dose or frequency changes. Phased oversight: physician pre-review of renewals for the first 250 patients (later changed to 250 fills per medication group), retrospective review of the next 1,000, then 5-10% monthly sampling. As of the state page, still in Phase 1 (physician reviews every renewal); Phase 2 requires OAIP approval.
drug_scope: Fixed formulary (~190 drugs, Schedule C) of chronic maintenance medications; controlled substances excluded; butalbital and flecainide later removed; limited refills per drug before a visit with a Utah-licensed clinician.
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: A Doctronic-employed/contracted Utah physician is the named prescriber on every AI renewal; Utah forgoes enforcement against that physician for being named without interacting with the patient (Sched. A s.15(D)). Company must carry malpractice insurance covering AI. State disclaims liability.
expiry: Register term 'October 24, 2025 - October 24, 2026'. A participant may ask for a 12-month extension no later than 30 days before the period ends; the office may grant at most two (register, citing Utah Code 13-72-403). Doctronic's own agreement (s.13) allows it to request a single extension of up to 12 months. As of 2026-11-12 the register (last modified 2026-10-06) still says Active and the pilot page (last modified 2026-06-18) says the office may 'review and renew the contract for another year'; no extension document is posted (WordPress media library checked for uploads since 2026-09-01).
legal_basis: Utah Code 13-72 (AI Policy Act; Learning Laboratory, regulatory mitigation s.13-72-302)
notes: Sched. A s.15(A): 'Participant may, using its artificial intelligence technology, authorize the renewal of a Utah resident's verified prescription to a pharmacist.' Medical board: letter dated 2026-04-20 from the Utah Medical Licensing Board: 'It is the strong recommendation of the Utah Medical Licensing Board that this program be immediately suspended pending further discussion'; it also said the board learned of the agreement only after the system was live and asked that professionals with medical backgrounds review proposals before implementation. DOPL and OAIP replied 2026-04-21 (letter signed by 11 of the board's 14 members, they wrote) that they would not suspend the pilot because Phase 1 has physician review of every refill; they also noted such board recommendations must come out of public meetings. The board's 2026-03-19 agenda lists 'AI Office - Doctronic' as a discussion item; no board minutes recording a vote were found. Contract amendment (2026): Phase 2 now gated per medication group (250 fills in that group) and still needs OAIP approval; butalbital and flecainide removed. First public report (2026-05-19, Jan-Apr data, Phase 1): AI recommended renewal in 72% of requests and escalated 28%; reviewing physician agreed with 91% of AI renewals (97% after a second physician opinion). Checked 2026-11-12.
short: Doctronic: renewals of existing prescriptions
review_now: A physician authorizes every renewal before it reaches the pharmacy.
next: Phase 2 (AI sends renewals, physicians review after the fact) needs Utah AI office approval, medication group by medication group; not approved.

status_detail: Approved, not started: the state register (last modified 2026-10-06) says 'The demonstration period has not started yet.' Press in April 2026 reported a launch; not reconciled with the register.
what_is_allowed: Legion Health's AI may authorize renewal of a Utah resident's verified existing psychiatric prescription and issue it to a Utah pharmacist. No diagnosis, new medications, or dose changes. Patients must be stable (no psychiatric hospitalization in past year per press). First 250 requests clinician-reviewed before completion, next 1,000 retrospectively reviewed, then monthly sampling.
drug_scope: Non-controlled psychiatric maintenance medications (common anxiety/depression treatments); controlled substances excluded.
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Affiliated provider acts as the 'named prescriber for such renewals' without interacting with the patient; Utah forgoes enforcement against that provider (Sched. A s.16(D)).
company_or_system: Legion Health (Legion Health, Inc. and Legion Health, PA)
start_date: Signed 2026-03-18/19; demonstration period not yet started per state register
notes: Agreement PDF is a scanned image; mitigation clause read from page 10 (Sched. A s.16). Register: a licensed clinician reviews the first 250 requests before any completes; the next 1,000 get intensive retrospective review; then monthly random sampling. Checked 2026-11-12.
short: Legion Health: psychiatric renewals
review_now: When it starts: a clinician reviews the first 250 requests before any completes.
next: Then 1,000 with review after the fact, then monthly sampling.

status_detail: Active (term 2026-10-05 to 2027-10-05 on the state register); Stage 1: two Utah-licensed physicians review every prescription before it is sent.
what_is_allowed: Nolla Health's AI (Nolla Skin app) may 'issue orders for first-time topical acne prescriptions and renewals to eligible Utah residents age 18 years and older' and transmit them to a Utah pharmacist, based on AI scoring of facial images. Stage 1 (min 4 weeks, 100 patients): two physicians review every prescription before submission. Stage 2 (min 8 weeks, 500 cumulative): AI submits directly, all cases reviewed retrospectively weekly. Stage 3 (750+): AI submits within scope, monthly review of at least 10%. Gates: >=95% concordance, zero missed hard stops, zero serious adverse events.
drug_scope: Topical acne products only (tretinoin, adapalene, clindamycin/benzoyl peroxide, azelaic acid, incl. compounded formulations with niacinamide/spironolactone); no oral or systemic therapy, no isotretinoin; adults with mild-moderate acne only. Controlled substances not relevant.
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Lead Utah-licensed physician oversees the program; Utah forgoes enforcement against affiliated providers who rely on the AI, including supervisors who 'may not be the individual treating provider of record' (Sched. A D). Company to carry pilot-specific professional liability coverage.
company_or_system: Nolla Health (Magic Health, Inc. / Magic Health Services, LLC)
notes: First state-sanctioned pilot found anywhere that authorizes AI-initiated (first-time) prescriptions, i.e. rung 3 on paper. Register (2026-10-06) lists it Active, in the first stage, so two physicians still review each prescription before it goes out; later stages need written OAIP approval. Checked 2026-11-12.
short: Nolla Health: first-time topical acne prescriptions
review_now: Two physicians review every prescription before it is sent.
next: Stage 2 (AI submits, weekly review of all cases after the fact) needs written approval after at least 4 weeks and 100 patients.

what_is_allowed: 'Artificial Intelligence Medical Services Act' (new Idaho Code Title 54, ch. 60) would license AAASPs with autonomy modifiers (L2 supervised, L3 fully autonomous AI authorized to 'independently diagnose, treat, triage, or prescribe'); licensees could issue orders for prescription drugs other than controlled substances within scope.
drug_scope: Prescription drugs other than controlled substances
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Licensed AAASP entity; professional liability insurance and tail coverage required; patient disclosure 'You are receiving care from an autonomous AI provider licensed by...'
start_date: Introduced 2026-03-25 by House Ways and Means; referred to Business
expiry: Idaho session adjourned 2026-04-02 with no further action
notes: Cicero Institute template, same structure as Iowa HSB 766. 'Failed' inferred from last action + sine die.
short: H 945, Artificial Intelligence Medical Services Act

what_is_allowed: Would create a board of autonomous medical practice licensing 'artificial intelligence augmented and autonomous service providers' (AAASPs, i.e. companies). 'Fully autonomous AI' = AI 'authorized to independently diagnose, treat, triage, or prescribe' without human supervision per case (s.153A.1(9)). L2/L3 licensees may issue medication orders 'other than controlled substances' within approved scope (s.153A.9).
drug_scope: Prescription drugs other than controlled substances
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: The licensed AAASP (a corporate entity) holds the license; provider-patient relationship and duty of care arise (s.153A.16(3)); malpractice coverage equivalent to a human specialist plus tail, surety bond >= $50,000; noneconomic damages capped for compliant provisional licensees.
expiry: No further action recorded; second session of the 91st General Assembly ended in 2026, so the study bill is dead
notes: Based on Cicero Institute model bill. Bill history page opened (last action 2026-03-24). Failed status inferred from no action before adjournment.
short: HSB 766, autonomous AI provider licensing

what_is_allowed: Healthy Technology Act of 2023: identical text to H.R. 238 (AI/ML as 'practitioner licensed by law' if state-authorized and FDA-authorized).
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: AI as practitioner
expiry: Died in committee at end of 118th Congress (Jan 2025)
notes: GovInfo BILLSTATUS (118th): introduced 2023-01-09, referred to Energy and Commerce, then to its Subcommittee on Health 2023-01-20 (last action); no cosponsors. Died at the end of the 118th Congress; Schweikert reintroduced it in 2025 as H.R. 238.
short: H.R. 206, Healthy Technology Act of 2023

what_is_allowed: Healthy Technology Act of 2025 would amend FDCA s.503(b) (21 U.S.C. 353(b)) so that 'practitioner licensed by law to administer such drug' includes AI/ML technology that is (A) authorized under a State statute to prescribe the drug and (B) FDA approved, cleared or authorized (510(k), 513, 515 or 564).
drug_scope: Any drug, as permitted by state law; silent on controlled substances (which separately need a DEA-registered individual practitioner).
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: AI itself would count as the practitioner for federal Rx-drug purposes; depends on a state statute authorizing it.
start_date: Introduced 2025-01-07; referred to House Energy and Commerce
expiry: Dies when the 119th Congress ends (early January 2027) unless passed. GovInfo bill-status file: latest action 2025-01-07, referred to House Energy and Commerce; no cosponsors listed.
notes: Sponsor Rep. David Schweikert (R-AZ). Status read from the GovInfo BILLSTATUS XML on 2026-11-12 (congress.gov returns 403).
short: H.R. 238, Healthy Technology Act of 2025

what_is_allowed: Health facilities, clinics, physician offices and group practices may not use AI to 'independently perform a clinical function that legally requires a professional license' or to direct unlicensed staff doing so; a licensed provider must keep independent professional judgment when care is informed by clinical decision support (Bus. & Prof. Code s.22758.5). Prescribing is a licensed function, so autonomous AI prescribing in those settings appears barred, though the law does not name prescribing.
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Licensed clinician
notes: Verified 2026-11-12 from the chaptered text (legislature bulk data, version 20250AB197989CHP): B&P s.22758.5(b)(1)(B), facilities, clinics, physician offices and group practices 'shall not use or deploy a tool, system, or device that includes artificial intelligence to ... (B) Independently perform any clinical function that is required by law to be performed by a person with a professional license.' Chapter 854, Statutes of 2026, approved 2026-09-30; no urgency clause, so effective 2027-01-01. Prescribing is not named, hence 'human must decide'. Whether it reaches direct-to-consumer AI companies that are not facilities or physician offices is unclear.
short: AB 1979, no AI performing licensed clinical functions on its own

what_is_allowed: B&P 4999.9: use of terms that imply 'the care, advice, reports, or assessments being offered through the AI or GenAI technology is being provided by a natural person in possession of the appropriate license ... is prohibited'; license-term bans are 'enforceable against a person or entity who develops or deploys' AI
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Developer or deployer; licensing boards, injunction under 125.5
notes: leginfo bill pages return 403; text verified from the legislature's bulk data file. Companion to known AB 1979 (Ch. 854, 2026, confirmed).
short: AB 489, no license-implying terms for AI

what_is_allowed: "A nonhuman entity, including an agent powered by artificial intelligence, may not be certified to practice medicine in the State" (24 Del. C. s.1720(k)); may not be licensed in professional nursing, as an APRN or in practical nursing (s.1920(h)) or as a physician assistant (s.1773(d)); may not use titles Dr., MD, DO, physician, APRN, CNP, RN, PA etc.
drug_scope: All (bars AI from holding the licenses that carry prescriptive authority)
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Only humans may hold the license
start_date: Approved 2026-04-23 (85 Del. Laws c. 250, formerly HB 191, 153rd GA)
notes: Opened the enrolled chapter law (Laws of Delaware vol. 85 ch. 250), hosted by Orrick rather than the state site. Clearest US statutory bar on AI holding a prescriber license (rung 4).
short: HB 191, no AI may be licensed as physician, nurse or PA

status_detail: Board of Nursing rules effective 2026-01-01, under HB 178 (Laws 2025 ch. 101, signed 2025-04-08), which added NMSA 61-3-10(Y)
what_is_allowed: 16.12.1.7: 'An artificial intelligence system shall not be labeled as or referred to as a nurse.' RN/APRN rules: 'The nurse remains accountable for decisions, actions, and intervention derived from or involving artificial intelligence'; 'AI shall be considered a decision-support tool. It may augment, but must not replace, the clinical reasoning and judgment of the [RN/APRN].'
drug_scope: All nursing practice including APRN prescribing
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Licensed nurse/APRN accountable
legal_basis: 16.12.1.7 NMAC (no 'nurse' label for AI); 16.12.16.13 (RN) and 16.12.17.12 (APRN) NMAC ('AI shall be considered a decision-support tool. It may augment, but must not replace...'); NMSA 61-3-10(Y) (HB 178, Chapter 101, signed April 8)
notes: Only board rule found that binds APRN prescribers to human judgment over AI. Nursing-title bar is comparable to Oregon ORS 678.027.
short: Nursing board rules: AI is decision support only

what_is_allowed: 'A nonhuman entity, including but not limited to an agent powered by artificial intelligence' may not use the titles nurse practitioner, APRN, CRNA, clinical nurse specialist, registered nurse, LPN, CMA or CNA.
drug_scope: Title protection only; indirectly bars AI from presenting as a nurse practitioner (a prescribing role).
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: n/a
notes: Title law, not a prescribing rule; include as a weak restriction or drop.
short: ORS 678.027, no nursing titles for AI

status_detail: Signed and effective 2026-04-23 (SB 837 as passed / HB 849); Pub. Ch. 781 assigned 2026-04-28
what_is_allowed: Clarifies that 'person', as used in Tennessee Code Annotated, 'does not include artificial intelligence, a computer algorithm, a software program, computer hardware, or any type of machine'
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Implicitly AI cannot be a licensed 'person' (prescriber) under TN practice acts
notes: General personhood definition, not a health statute. TN SB 1493 (Pub. Ch. 1066) was cut down to a TACIR study, so its AI-as-healthcare-professional felony was not enacted.
short: Pub. Ch. 781: AI is not a 'person' in state law

what_is_allowed: Practitioner may use AI for diagnostic purposes, including recommendations on diagnosis or treatment, only within scope of license, where not otherwise restricted, and must review AI-created records per Texas Medical Board standards; must disclose AI use to patients (Health & Safety Code s.183.005).
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: The practitioner
notes: Fact-check 2026-11-12: enrolled text s.183.005(a)(3) requires the practitioner to review all records created with AI; it does not separately require review of each recommendation. Effective 2025-09-01.
short: SB 1188, practitioner reviews AI-created records and discloses AI use

status_detail: professional ethics regulation binding physicians
what_is_allowed: AI is support only. The decision on diagnosis, prognosis, prescription or any medical act always rests with the physician (art. 18 s.2); AI may never restrict or replace the physician's final authority (art. 18 s.1); physicians may not delegate to AI the communication of diagnoses, prognoses or therapeutic decisions without human mediation (art. 5 s.2).
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Physician remains fully responsible (art. 7)
start_date: 2026-08-26 (signed 2026-02-11; in force 180 days after DOU publication 2026-02-27)
notes: Art. 18 §2: 'A decisão sobre diagnóstico, prognóstico, prescrição, ou qualquer ato médico, caberá sempre ao médico'. Binds physicians, not non-physician vendors.
short: Medical council Resolution 2,454/2026: prescription always rests with the physician

what_is_allowed: Nothing. Internet diagnosis and treatment prescriptions must be issued by the treating physician personally; AI auto-generating prescriptions is strictly prohibited, and AI software may not substitute for the physician.
drug_scope: All prescriptions issued in internet diagnosis/treatment
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Treating physician
start_date: 2022-02-08 (signed; posted on NHC site 2022-03-15; publicised June 2022)
legal_basis: Internet Diagnosis and Treatment Supervision Rules (Trial) (互联网诊疗监管细则（试行）), NHC General Office + NATCM Office, 国卫办医发〔2022〕2号, art. 13 and art. 21
notes: Fact-check 2026-11-12: primary source switched to the NHC Gazette PDF (2022 No.1, pp. 31-33), because the NHC notice page returns HTTP 412. Document 国卫办医发〔2022〕2号, dated 2022-02-08, a trial (试行) normative document. Art. 13: '其他人员、人工智能软件等不得冒用、替代医师本人提供诊疗服务' (other staff or AI software may not impersonate or replace the physician). Art. 21: '处方应由接诊医师本人开具，严禁使用人工智能等自动生成处方' (the treating physician must issue the prescription personally; using AI to auto-generate prescriptions is strictly prohibited). Arguably also restricts AI-drafted prescriptions (rung 1).
short: Internet diagnosis and treatment rules: no AI-generated prescriptions

status_detail: draft for comment (2023); final version not verified
what_is_allowed: Nothing. Prescription must be issued by the treating physician and pass pharmacist review; AI auto-generation strictly prohibited.
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Treating physician, plus pharmacist review
legal_basis: 北京市互联网诊疗监管实施办法（试行）(征求意见稿) art. 14, 22
notes: Source is Beijing Daily's report of the draft text.
short: Beijing internet care rules, 2023 draft

what_is_allowed: Nothing. Internet hospitals must route e-prescriptions through the provincial medical-insurance e-prescription centre and may not use AI to auto-generate prescriptions.
drug_scope: Prescriptions dispensed through medical-insurance designated retail pharmacies
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Physician
legal_basis: Hunan Healthcare Security Administration, 关于进一步加强基本医疗保障定点零售药店管理的通知 (湘医保发〔2025〕8号), section 二(五)
notes: Notice text opened on the Hunan HSA site 2026-11-12: internet hospitals '须按规定接入省医保电子处方中心并进行电子处方流转，处方行为须严格执行…《互联网诊疗监管细则（试行）》…等有关规定，应与患者或患者家属进行有效、充分的沟通问诊，严禁使用人工智能等自动生成处方。' Restates the 2022 national art. 21 for medical-insurance e-prescriptions. Earlier record cited only a newspaper page.
short: Hunan medical insurance notice

what_is_allowed: Nothing. AI/ML platforms may not counsel patients or prescribe; AI may assist the registered medical practitioner, but the final prescription must be delivered directly by the RMP.
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Registered Medical Practitioner
legal_basis: Telemedicine Practice Guidelines (Board of Governors in supersession of MCI), appended to IMC Professional Conduct Regulations
notes: 'Technology platforms based on Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning are not allowed to counsel the patients or prescribe any medicines to a patient. Only a RMP is entitled to counsel or prescribe.' Read on the NRCeS (MoHFW standards centre) page; the MoHFW PDF link no longer serves the PDF (checked 2026-11-12). Binding status rests on secondary sources: the IMC (Amendment) Regulations 2020 inserted reg. 3.8 making telemedicine permissible in accordance with Appendix 5 (these guidelines). The IMC Act has since been replaced by the NMC Act 2019; that the 2002 regulations still apply was not verified.
short: Telemedicine Practice Guidelines: AI may not prescribe

status_detail: national statute (Italian AI law), in force
what_is_allowed: AI systems in healthcare are support for prevention, diagnosis, treatment and therapeutic choice; the decision is always left to members of the medical profession. Patients have a right to be informed when AI is used (c.3); systems must be reliable and regularly checked (c.6).
drug_scope: All diagnostic and therapeutic decisions, incl. choice of therapy
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Physician ('esercenti la professione medica') keeps the decision
legal_basis: Legge 23 settembre 2025, n. 132 ('Disposizioni e deleghe al Governo in materia di intelligenza artificiale'), art. 7 c.5; GU n. 223 del 25-09-2025
notes: Art. 7 c.5: 'I sistemi di intelligenza artificiale in ambito sanitario costituiscono un supporto nei processi di prevenzione, diagnosi, cura e scelta terapeutica, lasciando impregiudicata la decisione, che è sempre rimessa agli esercenti la professione medica' (AI is support in prevention, diagnosis, care and therapeutic choice; the decision always rests with medical professionals). Text read on Normattiva (opening clause paraphrased by the fetch tool; the decision clause is verbatim). First EU member-state statute found that reserves therapeutic decisions to physicians by name. Binds the system generally, not only physicians; does not mention prescriptions or pharmacists. FNOMCeO and AIFA texts not checked (see leads).
short: Law 132/2025, art. 7: the decision always rests with physicians

status_detail: professional ethics code binding physicians (Kodeks Etyki Lekarskiej)
what_is_allowed: Physicians may use AI algorithms in diagnosis, treatment or prevention only if: the patient is informed, gives informed consent, the algorithm is approved for medical use and certified, and the final diagnostic and therapeutic decision is always taken by the physician.
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Physician
legal_basis: Kodeks Etyki Lekarskiej art. 12, as amended by the Extraordinary XVI National Congress of Physicians (Łódź, 2024)
notes: Art. 12 pkt 4: 'ostateczną decyzję diagnostyczną i terapeutyczną zawsze podejmuje lekarz' (the final diagnostic and therapeutic decision is always taken by the physician). Art. 12 also requires informing the patient and 'uzyskania świadomej zgody pacjenta na zastosowanie sztucznej inteligencji' (informed consent to AI use). Binds physicians, not platforms. The 2025 Polish crackdown on 'receptomaty' (e-prescription-by-questionnaire sites) was not verified (see leads).
short: Code of Medical Ethics, art. 12: the physician takes the final decision

jurisdiction: United States (FSMB, national model for state boards)
status_detail: Adopted by FSMB House of Delegates April 2024; no newer FSMB policy verified (fsmb.org pages 403)
what_is_allowed: AI is 'a tool to enhance, but generally not replace, human judgment and accountability'; tools 'have generally not been designed to, nor are they yet capable of, replacing a physician's professional judgment'; 'State medical boards do not regulate tools or technologies, only the licensed physicians that use those tools ... the physician is ultimately responsible'
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Physician
legal_basis: FSMB policy 'Navigating the Responsible and Ethical Incorporation of AI into Clinical Practice'
notes: Pre-2025, kept as baseline. PDF retrieved and read; confidence is medium only because it is model guidance, not state law.
short: Federation of State Medical Boards AI policy

what_is_allowed: Practitioners may use AI tools but must apply human judgment to AI output and remain responsible for care; TGA approval of a tool does not change the practitioner's oversight duty; informed consent and transparency expected. Prescribing and autonomous AI not addressed.
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Registered practitioner
legal_basis: Ahpra / National Boards, Meeting your professional obligations when using AI in healthcare
notes: 'the practitioner remains responsible for delivering safe and quality care'; 'TGA approval of a tool does not change a practitioner's responsibility' to apply human oversight. Not prescription-specific; loosely meets the rung-1 test like jp-mhlw-ai-notice-2018. No 2025-2026 revision seen on the page. Merged with duplicate record au-ahpra-ai-guidance-2024 from a second research pass.
short: Ahpra: the practitioner stays responsible for AI output

status_detail: Board guidelines, not AI-specific; not binding in themselves, but admissible as evidence of professional standards in disciplinary proceedings (Health Practitioner Regulation National Law s.41)
what_is_allowed: Prescribing without a real-time direct consultation, including on asynchronous requests by text, email, live chat or online questionnaire where the practitioner has never spoken with the patient, is 'not good practice and is not supported by the Board'. Exception: the patient's usual practitioner, or one with access to the clinical record, may sometimes prescribe without a consultation. Effectively blocks questionnaire-driven (and so automated) prescribing for new patients.
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Registered medical practitioner; must be able to explain why prescribing without consultation was appropriate
expiry: Review at least every five years
legal_basis: Medical Board of Australia, Guidelines: Telehealth consultations with patients (replace 2012 technology-based consultation guidelines); Health Practitioner Regulation National Law s.39
notes: Board page (reviewed 1/09/2023): 'Prescribing or providing healthcare for a patient without a real-time direct consultation ... is not good practice and is not supported by the Board', covering requests 'based on the patient completing a health questionnaire' where the practitioner 'has never spoken with the patient'. No AI mention. Oct 2025 Ahpra cross-profession telehealth update reported (press only, not opened) to restate this. No 2026 Board AI or async update found, but searching was cut short. Merged with duplicate record au-mba-telehealth-async-prescribing from a second research pass.
short: Medical Board telehealth guidelines: no questionnaire-only prescribing

status_detail: compliance guide (合规指南), 4 chapters, 42 articles; guidance, not a binding regulation
what_is_allowed: No AI prescription review on the dispensing side. Online prescription-drug retailers must have prescription review done by licensed pharmacists, 'not by other staff or by artificial intelligence'. Sixth Tone also reports that platforms 'cannot use AI to review, approve, or renew prescriptions'; that renewal wording is not in the Chinese sources opened, and Caixin's English report does not mention renewal either. Caixin adds that platforms must use technology to identify and block AI-generated and fake prescriptions.
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Licensed pharmacists for review; prescriber unchanged
legal_basis: NMPA, 《处方药网络零售合规指南》 (Prescription Drug Online Retail Compliance Guide), issued 2026-05-25
notes: Xinhua (2026-05-26, Economic Information Daily): '药品网络零售企业要确保本企业的处方审核工作由执业药师开展，不得由其他岗位人员或者人工智能代为实施' (prescription review must be done by licensed pharmacists, not by other staff or AI). The NMPA policy interpretation reprinted by Xinhua (2026-05-25) gives the title and structure and does not mention renewal. The guide text itself is still not opened (nmpa.gov.cn returns HTTP 412 to scripts). So the AI-review ban is confirmed in Chinese state media; the rung-2 'renew' reading rests on Sixth Tone alone. Checked 2026-11-12.
short: Online prescription drug retail guide: no AI prescription review

status_detail: statement of the German Medical Association board (not binding law; professional codes are set by the Land chambers)
what_is_allowed: AI may support physicians, but responsibility for diagnosis, indication and therapy is always a medical task and may not be ceded to an AI system; physicians must check AI output for plausibility.
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Physician; statement calls for clear rules on when the manufacturer vs. the physician/facility is liable
legal_basis: BÄK Stellungnahme 'Künstliche Intelligenz in der Medizin' (Dtsch Arztebl 2025, DOI 10.3238/arztebl.2025.Stellungnahme_KI_Medizin); background: AMVV §2(1) Nr. 1 and 10
notes: p.8: 'KI kann die ärztliche Tätigkeit unterstützen, aber die Verantwortung für Diagnostik, Indikationsstellung und Therapie ist stets ärztliche Aufgabe und darf nicht an ein KI-System abgetreten werden' (responsibility for diagnosis, indication and therapy is always the physician's and may not be ceded to AI); repeated in the recommendations section. 128th Deutscher Ärztetag 2024 resolution Ic-87 (adopted 157-18-18): 'KI kann den Arzt/die Ärztin unterstützen und entlasten, darf ihn/sie aber nicht ersetzen' and 'KI-Empfehlungen darf nicht "blind gefolgt" werden'. Neither text names prescriptions. Structural barrier (not AI-specific): AMVV §2(1) requires the name and Berufsbezeichnung of the 'verschreibenden Person' (Nr. 1) and 'die eigenhändige Unterschrift der verschreibenden Person' or 'deren qualifizierte elektronische Signatur' (Nr. 10), so an E-Rezept needs a human prescriber's QES.
short: German Medical Association: therapy decisions may not be ceded to AI

what_is_allowed: AI diagnosis/treatment-support programs may be used, but the physician is the agent of diagnosis and treatment and bears final responsibility; such care is medical practice under Medical Practitioners Act art. 17.
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Physician
legal_basis: MHLW notice 医政医発1219第1号
notes: Not prescription-specific; loosely meets the rung-1 inclusion test.
short: Health ministry notice: the physician decides and is responsible

what_is_allowed: AI may support a doctor only within the doctor's scope; 'AI is not a substitute for your clinical judgement, and you remain responsible for all your clinical decisions and actions.' Doctors 'must not use AI to impersonate yourself in medical practice, including through avatars or chatbots'; registration and practising certificate 'cannot be transferred to an AI system'. Patients must be told explicitly about high-risk AI that influences clinical decisions; informed consent needed where AI plays a significant role in treatment.
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Registered doctor. Separately, Council's prescribing statement says the doctor who signs a repeat prescription takes responsibility for it, and Medicines Regulations 1984 reg. 39 bars prescribing except for a patient under the doctor's care.
legal_basis: Medical Council of New Zealand, Guidance on using artificial intelligence (AI) in patient care (March 2026), paras 4, 6, 7, 9; Statement on good prescribing practice (Feb 2024) paras 2, 34-35
notes: Soft-law guidance against rungs 2-4; nearest NZ analogue to Singapore AIHGle. Not prescription-specific, but para 6 (registration cannot transfer to AI) is the clearest regulator line in the region that an AI cannot be the practitioner. Prescribing statement para 35: patients needing assessment 'should not receive repeat prescriptions without being seen by a doctor'. Near-neighbour: a Director-General waiver lets NZePS 'Signature Exempt Prescriptions' be issued electronically without the prescriber's personal signature (still prescriber-issued).
short: Medical Council: registration cannot transfer to an AI

what_is_allowed: Human-in-the-loop or supervised AI only. Deployers 'should not deploy AI solutions that make clinical decisions independently without human making the final decision'; 'autonomous AI should not be deployed without human oversight'. Medication-dosing recommendation software listed as clinical-risk AI; an AI robot that reads prescriptions and dispenses without human oversight is given as an example not to deploy.
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Healthcare professionals 'remain responsible ... regardless of whether AI solutions are used' (s.7.1.1)
legal_basis: MOH/HSA AI in Healthcare Guidelines 2.0 (Version 2.0, March 2026) s.6.2.2-6.2.3
notes: Soft-law guidance against rungs 2-4.
short: AI in Healthcare Guidelines 2.0: a human makes the final decision

status_detail: regulator guidance for registered pharmacies (owners/superintendents); used as the standard in GPhC inspections and fitness-to-practise
what_is_allowed: Online/distance pharmacies may not supply listed higher-risk medicines on a questionnaire-only prescribing model. For those medicines the prescriber must not base the decision on the questionnaire alone and must independently verify the patient's information (two-way communication, clinical records, or contact with the GP/regular prescriber), make a contemporaneous record justifying the decision, and redirect the patient if verification fails. For long-term conditions the prescriber must verify medical history with the GP/regular prescriber or records before supply. Not AI-specific, but it blocks fully automated questionnaire-to-prescription flows for these drug classes.
drug_scope: Antimicrobials; medicines liable to misuse (opioids, sedatives, laxatives, gabapentinoids, stimulants, nootropics); overdose-risk drugs (e.g. amitriptyline, propranolol, colchicine, carbamazepine); narrow therapeutic index and long-term-condition medicines (diabetes, asthma, epilepsy, heart conditions, mental health); pregnancy prevention programme drugs; weight-management medicines; non-surgical cosmetic medicines; black-triangle medicines
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Human prescriber (doctor or non-medical independent prescriber) makes and records the decision; the pharmacy owner/superintendent must be assured the prescribing service has these safeguards
legal_basis: Pharmacy Order 2010; GPhC Standards for registered pharmacies; GPhC Guidance for registered pharmacies providing pharmacy services at a distance, including on the internet (Feb 2025)
notes: Para j: 'Some medicines are not suitable to be prescribed by a questionnaire model alone.' Para k: 'The prescriber does not base prescribing decisions on the information provided in a questionnaire alone. Instead, the prescriber independently verifies the information the person provides ...' and 'If the prescriber cannot independently verify the information ... the person should be directed to an appropriate care provider'. No mention of AI or algorithms; rung '2-4' is inferred because a questionnaire-only (including automated/AI) prescribing path is blocked for the listed classes. GMC 'Good practice in proposing, prescribing, providing and managing medicines and devices' (remote prescribing paragraphs) is the doctor-side counterpart but gmc-uk.org returned 403 and was not opened.
short: Pharmacy regulator: no questionnaire-only prescribing for listed medicines

status_detail: SD1 passed second reading 2026-02-18; referred to CPN/WAM; never passed Senate; died at adjournment
what_is_allowed: Provider using AI as 'a substantial factor in making, a consequential decision' must have 'artificial intelligence oversight personnel' who 'shall be a natural person' and 'Validate or override the output'; patient notice, opt-out and human-review appeal
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Provider; DOH rulemaking
notes: Secondary trackers wrongly say it passed the Senate.
short: SB 2281, a person validates or overrides AI decisions

status_detail: HB 4804 (Rep. Morgan) re-referred to Rules 2026-03-27 (Rule 19(a)); SB 3702 (Sen. Guzmán) re-referred to Assignments 2026-05-22 (Rule 3-9(a)). 104th GA runs to Jan 2027
what_is_allowed: Amends Nurse Practice Act: 'prohibition on substituting artificial intelligence for nursing services; use of artificial intelligence as clinical decision support under the control of a registered professional nurse'; health care entities must 'prohibit staffing, triage, admission, discharge, or transfer decisions that rely solely on artificial intelligence'
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: RN; IDFPR discipline
notes: Quoted language is from the ILGA synopsis, not the bill text.
short: HB 4804 / SB 3702, AI may not substitute for nursing

status_detail: pending; re-referred to Assignments 2026-05-22 (Rule 3-9(a)); alive until the 104th General Assembly ends in January 2027
what_is_allowed: Would amend the Medical Practice Act to prohibit a licensee from 'allowing artificial intelligence to prescribe medication' unless the licensee maintains full control and responsibility for the prescription; penalties; IDFPR rulemaking on authorized AI prescribing.
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Licensed physician must retain full control and responsibility.
notes: Conditional, not a flat ban: Sec. 7.3(a) reads 'No person licensed under this Act shall allow artificial intelligence to prescribe medication if the person licensed under this Act does not maintain full control and responsibility for the prescription', and IDFPR would make rules on the authorized use of AI to prescribe. Opened via curl (ilga.gov certificate error in fetch tool).
short: SB 2993, no AI prescribing without physician control

status_detail: AI clause in introduced version (2026-01-05) removed by committee substitute 2026-01-14; SB 180 later enacted as a health omnibus without AI language
what_is_allowed: Proposed IC 25-1-23.5-4: 'A person or entity may not use an artificial intelligence system to: (1) impersonate; or (2) act as a substitute for; a licensed practitioner during any interaction that is required to be performed by the licensed practitioner.'
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Licensee discipline under IC 25-1-9
short: SB 180 as introduced, AI may not substitute for a practitioner

status_detail: Introduced 2026-01-28; hearing 2026-02-09 (AG Kobach for); died in committee
what_is_allowed: Unlawful to knowingly train AI to 'act as or provide information as if the artificial intelligence is a licensed mental health or healthcare professional'
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: AG or private action; $150,000 liquidated damages
notes: Mainly a chatbot bill; included for the healthcare-professional impersonation bar.
short: SB 405, AI may not pose as a healthcare professional

status_detail: 2026 RS; prefiled 2026-02-18 (Rep. Domangue); referred to House Health and Welfare 2026-03-09; no hearing; NCSL 'Failed - Adjourned'
what_is_allowed: Proposed R.S. 37:22.1(C): 'A healthcare provider shall not utilize artificial intelligence without review and approval by a licensed healthcare professional to do any of the following: (1) Make a decision related to treatment or diagnosis. (2) Interact directly with a patient in any form of communication. (3) Generate a therapeutic recommendation or treatment plan.' Administrative uses allowed.
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Provider; $10,000 per violation; LDH enforcement and referral to licensing boards
notes: LA HB 475 (Act 649, 2026) is disclosure-only and was not included.
short: HB 197, licensed review before AI treatment decisions

status_detail: HF 4979 introduced 2026-04-16 to House Commerce; companion SF 4927 introduced 2026-03-26; no further action; 2026 session ended
what_is_allowed: Proposed 325F.701 'PROHIBITION ON ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE PERFORMING LICENSED ACTIVITIES': 'The owner of an artificial intelligence model is prohibited from allowing the model to provide a professional service to a consumer unless the model is operated, while the service is being provided, by a natural person who is credentialed to provide the professional services'; credentialed professionals may use AI 'as a tool'.
drug_scope: All state-licensed services (medicine, nursing, pharmacy implied)
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Attorney General enforcement under 8.31
notes: Not tagged Health Use in NCSL.
short: HF 4979, AI may not provide a professional service on its own

status_detail: 2026; referred to House Public Health 2026-01-19; died in committee 2026-02-03
what_is_allowed: Clinical AI that 'materially contributes to a diagnosis, treatment plan, problem list entry, order or clinical note' requires 'clinical attestation through an electronic signature by a licensed clinician accepting or rejecting the AI suggestion prior to finalizing'; 'AI that automatically inserts diagnoses or orders into a chart ... without clinician acceptance is prohibited'; 'AI outputs are advisory only'
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Treating clinician keeps 'ultimate authority'; audit log; licensing-board enforcement
legal_basis: Proposed Mississippi Medical Judgment Protection Act (amends Miss. Code 73-25-29 et al.)
notes: Effectively a per-order human-signature (rung-1) mandate.
short: HB 1717, clinician signs every AI order

status_detail: SS#2/SCS/SB 1012 (AI Non-Sentience and Responsibility Act) perfected and passed the Senate; House committee 'Motion to Do Pass Failed' 2026-05-12; session ended 2026-05-15
what_is_allowed: Sec. 1.2045.9(1)(a): 'A licensed professional rendering a regulated service shall exercise independent professional judgment and retain final authority over any determination, diagnosis, recommendation, or decision ... including for the purpose of dispensing, prescribing, renewing any prescription of, administering, or otherwise distributing medications or controlled substances, regardless of whether an AI system was used to assist in its preparation.' (e): no one may represent that an AI system 'is or is capable of acting as a licensed professional'. Also declares AI non-sentient with no legal personhood.
drug_scope: All medications and controlled substances, renewals included
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Licensed professional bears responsibility for AI mistakes as if AI were not used; failure to exercise independent judgment is grounds for board discipline; 'An AI system shall not be held liable'
notes: Introduced version was a deepfake bill; the AI/prescribing text came in the Senate substitute. 'Regulated service' list includes physicians (MD/DO), RNs, dentists, optometrists, podiatrists, psychologists and physical therapists (pharmacists included; the list also covers counselors, veterinarians and chiropractors, among others). Not tagged by NCSL.
short: SB 1012, professional keeps final authority over prescribing and renewals

status_detail: Introduced 2026-02-26 (Sen. Beck); no committee action; died when the session's bill-passing deadline passed (2026-05-15)
what_is_allowed: Proposed RSMo 324.049: the board of registration for the healing arts, dental board, board of nursing and board of pharmacy 'shall not grant any regulatory mitigation or waive or modify any rules related to dispensing, prescribing, including prescription renewals, administering, or otherwise distributing medications or controlled substances to a person or business developing, creating, or generating artificial intelligence for the use of dispensing, prescribing, including prescription renewals...'
drug_scope: All medications and controlled substances, renewals expressly included
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: n/a (bars sandbox or waiver relief; human prescribers remain the only lawful prescribers)
notes: Direct legislative response to Utah-style 'regulatory mitigation' agreements for AI renewals. It bars boards from granting waivers or sandbox relief for AI prescribing, the only route around human-only prescribing, rather than regulating AI use directly. AI is defined as conversational GenAI producing outputs 'with limited or no human oversight'.
short: SB 1804, no waivers for AI prescribing or renewals

status_detail: Passed Senate with amendment 2026-1051s (2026-03-12, voice vote); House ED&A committee report Inexpedient to Legislate 11-1; House ITL 2026-05-14
what_is_allowed: Repeal and reenact RSA 310:13 'Unlicensed Practice; Use of Artificial Intelligence': bill analysis says it 'Prohibits the use of artificial intelligence or other means to provide services requiring a professional license unless those services are provided by someone with such a license'; unlicensed practice by 'individuals and entities' carries a $10,000 civil penalty per violation. Para. III adds mental-health-specific AI limits.
drug_scope: All professions under NH OPLC (which covers medicine, nursing and pharmacy boards); prescribing not named
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Unlicensed-practice penalty against the entity; licensee remains responsible
notes: Senate sponsors were bipartisan (11 senators).
short: SB 640, no AI providing licensed services

status_detail: 222nd Legislature; introduced 2026-10-05 (Sen. Owen Henry); referred to Senate Commerce Committee; no later action
what_is_allowed: Unauthorized practice of any Title 45 profession 'shall include the production of content by artificial intelligence or generative artificial intelligence. Any person or entity that deploys ... or ... develops an artificial intelligence ... system, shall be considered to have engaged in the unauthorized practice of a profession'. Licensees may use AI if output is labeled with a disclaimer.
drug_scope: All Title 45 professions (Board of Medical Examiners, Nursing, Pharmacy); prescribing implied
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: AI developer or deployer = unauthorized practitioner; licensee in good standing exempt with disclosure
notes: Pending; NJ session runs to Jan 2028.
short: S4754, AI output counts as unlicensed practice

status_detail: Introduced 2025-02-03; referred to House Rules 2025-02-04; no action through end of 2026 session
what_is_allowed: 'An AI device shall be used exclusively by a qualified end-user' (licensed physician); 'All relevant AI device-generated data shall be reviewed for accuracy and validated by a qualified end-user ... before patient care decisions are rendered'
drug_scope: FDA-defined AI/ML devices for diagnosis, prognosis or treatment
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Physician end-user decides; deployer QA program; State Dept. of Health enforces
short: HB 1915, physician validates AI output before care decisions

status_detail: 2026; referred to Senate Health and Human Services 2026-02-03; no further action
what_is_allowed: Sec. 3: 'A licensed health care provider shall not allow artificial intelligence to ... 1. Make independent medical decisions; 2. Directly interact with patients ...; 3. Diagnose medical conditions; or 4. Generate medical advice or recommendations or treatment plans without review by the licensed health care provider.' 'A licensed health care provider, not artificial intelligence or similar systems, shall make final decisions'. Written informed consent required for AI use.
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Provider 'maintains full responsibility'; board discipline up to $10,000 per violation
short: SB 2037, a licensed provider makes final decisions

status_detail: Passed House 144-59 on 2026-09-30 (PN 3963); referred to Senate Institutional Sustainability and Innovation 2026-10-14. Senate counterpart SB 1113 (PN 1376) in the same Senate committee since 2026-01-09
what_is_allowed: Facilities using AI for clinical decision making: 'The artificial intelligence model or system for clinical decision making must not supersede clinical decision making made by a human health care provider. A facility may not penalize a health care provider solely for exercising independent judgment ... that differs from a recommendation or output generated by artificial intelligence.' Annual DOH compliance statements.
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Human provider; facility compliance to DOH
legal_basis: Proposed 35 Pa.C.S. ch. 35 (also 40 and 67 Pa.C.S. for insurers and MA/CHIP)
notes: Live: the session runs through Nov 2026 and the bill dies at session end if the Senate doesn't act.
short: HB 1925, AI may not supersede a clinician's decision

status_detail: PN 3721; referred to House Professional Licensure 2026-06-29
what_is_allowed: Each licensing board 'shall establish rules addressing the use of artificial intelligence by licensees', including 'Limitations ... that artificial intelligence may not independently perform professional services, make professional decisions, establish a professional relationship or fulfill a duty imposed on a licensee under the applicable practice act'
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Licensee
short: HB 2678, boards must bar AI from acting independently

status_detail: AL HB 280 / SB 97 (2026) and KY SB 175 (2026): both died in committee
what_is_allowed: Same model bill, a state 'Health Command' AI-assisted virtual health platform. AL text: 'does not include the diagnosis, treatment, or prescription of medical conditions'. KY: platform must 'Not include or engage in the practice of medicine or the diagnosis or treatment of any disease'.
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Licensed clinicians via telehealth escalation
legal_basis: Proposed uncodified AL act; proposed KRS 42.720-42.742 amendments
short: State AI health platform bills that excluded prescribing

status_detail: Attorney General's regulatory sandbox, open to 'other innovations' since 2022 (HB 2731); participants page reads 'No Current Participants'
what_is_allowed: Admitted participants may test innovative financial products or 'other innovations' with limited access to the Arizona market without first obtaining full state licensure, for up to two years, after the AG consults the relevant agencies. No AI prescribing participant is listed.
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Not specified
company_or_system: None (press: Doctronic applied, per Bloomberg Law, June 2026)
notes: Participants page fetched 2026-11-12: 'No Current Participants.' The claimed 'Arizona SB 1847' on prescription renewals does not match the legislature's record: 2026 SB 1847 is the general appropriations act for 2026-2027 (signed 2026-06-13, chapter 126); its text was not read for AI provisions. Arizona HB 4080 (2026, AI nursing-tasks pilot) was held in Rules.
short: Attorney General's regulatory sandbox

status_detail: Not yet a bill: Legislative Council draft for the interim AI and Data Center Committee, Oct 2026, aimed at the 2027 session
what_is_allowed: Regulatory sandbox to 'test innovative artificial intelligence systems for a limited amount of time without obtaining a license, registration, or other regulatory authorization', 'across various sectors including healthcare'; up to 36 months; agencies may not discipline for waived-law violations
drug_scope: Not specified; does not expressly waive medical, nursing or pharmacy practice acts
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Not specified
legal_basis: Proposed new sections in NDCC ch. 54-59 (sandbox); ch. 51-40 (AI disclosures)
notes: Watch for 2027 introduction. Status value is an approximation: it is not yet introduced.
short: AI sandbox draft for the 2027 session

what_is_allowed: Texas Responsible AI Governance Act (HB 149) creates a regulatory sandbox run by the Department of Information Resources: approved participants may test AI for up to 36 months with 'certain laws and regulations related to the testing' waived or suspended; health care is listed among target sectors and there is no carve-out for medical licensing, but applicable agencies must approve. Also requires disclosure of AI use in health care services (s.552.051).
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Not specified
company_or_system: None confirmed for prescribing (press: Doctronic in talks with Texas)
notes: Enabling framework only; no AI prescribing participant found. DIR pages return 403 to scripts. Secondary sources (Chambers practice guide, May 2026; a TRAIGA explainer citing a 2026-11-04 check) found no adopted DIR rule, application form or participant for the private-sector sandbox. DIR's separate public-sector AI sandbox works with state agencies only. Doctronic has said it is in talks with Texas (press). Checked 2026-11-12.
short: AI regulatory sandbox (HB 149)

status_detail: implicit prohibition for controlled substances
what_is_allowed: 'A prescription for a controlled substance may be issued only by an individual practitioner' who is state-authorized and either DEA-registered or exempted from registration (21 CFR 1306.03(a)); an individual practitioner is a physician, dentist, veterinarian or other licensed individual (21 CFR 1300.01). Ryan Haight Act requires an in-person evaluation for internet prescribing, with exceptions. AI cannot be an individual practitioner, which is why the Utah pilots and the Iowa and Idaho bills exclude controlled substances; H.R. 238 is silent on them, but this rule would still apply.
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Individual DEA-registered practitioner
notes: Not AI-specific; context row explaining the universal controlled-substance carve-out.
short: DEA rule: controlled-substance prescriptions need an individual practitioner

what_is_allowed: FDA's Clinical Decision Support Software guidance (Jan 29, 2026) treats software as non-device CDS only if it supports an HCP, does not give a specific treatment directive, is 'not intended to replace or direct the HCP's judgment', and lets the HCP independently review the basis (FD&C Act s.520(o)(1)(E)). Patient-facing software or software that autonomously decides treatment does not qualify, so an autonomous prescribing AI would be a regulated medical device. FDA told AP (July 2026) it has authorized no AI chatbots; none of the Utah pilots has disclosed FDA authorization.
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: n/a (device regulation)
notes: Interpretation (that autonomous prescribing AI falls outside non-device CDS) is ours, from the guidance's Criterion 3/4 text; FDA has not issued anything prescribing-specific.
short: FDA clinical decision support guidance

what_is_allowed: Master regulatory mitigation agreements with University of Utah Health (signed 2026-09-10) and Intermountain Health (Sept 2026) set terms for future AI pilots approved one by one via addenda; no pilots approved yet.
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Not yet defined
company_or_system: University of Utah Health; Intermountain Health
expiry: Open-ended; each pilot 12 months plus up to two 12-month extensions
notes: Context only; not prescribing yet. Downloaded U of U master agreement but read only the register summary of it.
short: Master agreements with University of Utah Health and Intermountain

what_is_allowed: Pharmacists may dispense an emergency refill of a non-controlled medication the patient is on and that is on file, without prescriber authorization, for a 30-day supply or the last quantity dispensed (Utah Admin. Code R156-17b-612(14); Utah Code 58-17b-608). Utah's AI office cites this, and similar 'Kevin's Law' rules in most states, as precedent for limited-information AI renewals.
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Pharmacist
notes: Near-neighbour tied to AI by the OAIP memo; rule text itself not opened.
short: Pharmacist emergency refill rule

status_detail: 2026 HB 146 (Williams) left in House Health and Human Services 2026-02-18; same model as 2025 HB 1555 (failed 9-12)
what_is_allowed: VDH 'Health Care Learning Lab and Regulatory Improvement Program' sandbox for innovations 'including artificial intelligence', testing 'without obtaining a license' for 24 (+6) months, but 'Nothing in this chapter shall be construed to waive any ... Licensure, certification, or registration requirement of any health regulatory board ... related to the practice of any health care provider with prescriptive authority'
drug_scope: Prescribing expressly excluded from sandbox relief
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Human prescribers only
notes: A health sandbox that carves out prescribing, the opposite of Utah's design.
short: HB 146, health sandbox that excluded prescribers

status_detail: Introduced 2024, continued to 2025; left in House General Laws
what_is_allowed: DPOR regulatory boards may 'promulgate regulations ... for an applicant requesting licensure of an autonomous agent', defined as 'software or hardware that operates independently, without real-time human intervention, and is capable of performing tasks that, when executed by a human, would require licensure'
drug_scope: None (DPOR boards only; medicine, nursing and pharmacy boards sit under DHP and are not covered)
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Owner or operator holds the license
notes: Rung-4-style AI licensure concept, but outside health care. source_date is approximate (2025 session end).
short: HB 248, licensing 'autonomous agents' (non-health boards)

status_detail: Medical Digital Innovation Sandbox Act (2019 SF 156); Department of Health rules effective 2020-02-06; application form updated Feb 2026; no participant list published
what_is_allowed: The Wyoming Department of Health may grant waivers of statutes and rules so a person can offer an 'innovative medical digital assessment product or service' to consumers; the relevant licensing board must grant the waiver, then a review committee advises the Director. Sandbox period up to 24 months, extension up to 12. Applicants must be domestic entities with a physical presence in Wyoming and post a consumer protection bond.
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Not specified
company_or_system: None found (press: Doctronic in talks with Wyoming officials)
legal_basis: W.S. 40-28-101 to -108; Wyo. Dept. of Health rules ch. 1
notes: Existing health sandbox that could in principle host an AI prescribing waiver, but only if a licensing board grants it. The Department's page (modified 2026-03-04) lists no participants and no AI prescribing waiver was found. AP and Snell & Wilmer reports of Wyoming 'waiving rules for AI in health care' and a sandbox 'in development' were not matched to any agreement. Checked 2026-11-12.
short: Medical Digital Innovation Sandbox Act

what_is_allowed: No prescribing provision. Class II-IV machine-learning-enabled medical devices must disclose ML use, may file a predetermined change control plan (PCCP), must describe how output fits the clinical workflow and the device's degree of autonomy, and address automation bias. Any AI prescribing tool qualifying as a device would go through this route.
drug_scope: Any AI prescribing system qualifying as a medical device
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Not addressed; prescriber authority set by provincial law and colleges
legal_basis: Medical Devices Regulations (SOR/98-282); Health Canada Pre-market guidance for machine learning-enabled medical devices
notes: Context row like eu-ai-act. Defines autonomy as 'the capacity to perform a clinical function with no or limited user intervention'; flags automation bias. Prescribing not mentioned. Page shows 'Date published: April 1, 2026' (earlier draft 2023).
short: Health Canada guidance on machine-learning devices

status_detail: Lapsed: art. 52 says the rules take effect on issue and are valid for 2 years (有效期 2 年), so they ran to 2026-02-08; no renewal found as of 2026-11-12. Kept as context, not counted on the wall.
what_is_allowed: Nothing. AI software may not impersonate or replace the physician in diagnosis, prescribing or follow-up; AI auto-generated prescriptions strictly prohibited.
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Treating physician
expiry: 2026-02-08 (2-year validity per art. 52; renewal not verified)
notes: Art. 14: '其他人员、人工智能软件等不得冒用、替代医师本人提供诊断、开方、随访等诊疗服务'. Art. 20: '严禁使用人工智能等自动生成处方'. Art. 52: '本办法自印发之日起施行，有效期 2 年。' Example of a province copying the national clause. Moved off the wall in the 2026-11-12 fact-check because it appears to have lapsed.
short: Fujian internet care rules, lapsed February 2026

status_detail: as amended by the Digital Omnibus on AI, Regulation (EU) 2026/1744
what_is_allowed: No prescribing-specific provision. AI that is, or is a safety component of, a medical device needing third-party conformity assessment under MDR/IVDR is high-risk (art. 6(1), Annex I) and must allow effective human oversight, incl. ability to 'disregard, override or reverse the output' (art. 14(4)(d)).
drug_scope: Any AI prescribing system qualifying as a medical device
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Not addressed; prescriber rules set by member states and Directive 2001/83/EC
start_date: 2024-08-01; art. 6(1)/Annex I high-risk obligations from 2028-08-02 (moved from 2027-08-02 by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744); Annex III from 2027-12-02
legal_basis: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 arts. 6, 14, 113, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 art. 1(40)
notes: Context row: regulates rung 2-4 systems but neither permits nor bans them. Digital Omnibus on AI (procedure 2025/0359(COD), COM(2025) 836): proposed 2025-11-19, EP first reading 2026-06-16, Council 2026-06-29, signed 2026-07-08, OJ 2026-07-24, in force 2026-07-27. New art. 113(b): '2 December 2027 as regards AI systems classified as high-risk pursuant to Article 6(2) and Annex III' and '2 August 2028 as regards AI systems classified as high-risk pursuant to Article 6(1) and Annex I'. Fixed dates, not tied to standards. Art. 14 not amended; MDR/IVDR stay in Annex I Section A (only machinery moved to Section B). Full-text check of the original Act: no recital, article or annex mentions medical prescriptions, prescribing or medicinal products ('prescribe' appears only for market-surveillance deadlines). Directive 2001/83/EC art. 1(19): 'Medicinal Prescription: Any medicinal prescription issued by a professional person qualified to do so' (who qualifies is left to member states).
short: EU AI Act

what_is_allowed: AI 'Dr. Hua' interviews the patient and generates a diagnosis and treatment plan (including prescriptions); a licensed doctor reviews and approves each plan, without an in-person visit. Data collected toward Saudi regulatory approval.
drug_scope: About 30 respiratory conditions, planned expansion to ~50 (respiratory, GI, derm); controlled substances not stated
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Licensed physician approves each plan
company_or_system: Synyi AI with Almoosa Health Group
notes: Widely billed as an 'AI doctor clinic' but it is rung 1.
short: Private AI clinic pilot, a doctor signs each plan

status_detail: framework for research; nothing authorised yet
what_is_allowed: Framework for researching 'AI clinician systems' that 'may ultimately be authorised to perform clinical activities that would otherwise require a licensed clinician', with physician oversight and accountability and referral to a physician when needed; future DoH policies to define permitted activities. Research stage only; prescribing not mentioned.
drug_scope: Not specified; prescribing not named in reports
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Physician oversight and accountability and referral to a physician required at all scope levels
notes: Only non-US regulator announcement found that envisions AI holding clinician-equivalent authorisation (a rung-4 pathway). Primary source switched to TradeArabia (2026-10-21) because the WAM page loads without body text; framework document itself not found.
short: AI Clinician Framework, research stage

status_detail: regulator guidance on how existing medical device law applies; does not change the law
what_is_allowed: Ambient voice tech (AI scribe) used only to transcribe, summarise, draft letters or suggest codes for clinician review is not a medical device. AVT that structures encounter data into medication lists or order sets for a clinician to review, edit and confirm is treated as administrative. AVT that autonomously decides on follow-up and places orders without clinician input or confirmation is a medical device and must meet device safety/performance requirements (UKCA/CE). Not banned, but regulated as a device.
drug_scope: Orders generally (example given is follow-up tests); medicines not singled out
legal_basis: UK Medical Devices Regulations 2002 (as applied by MHRA); MHRA 'Guidance on Ambient Voice Technology-Enabled Products: Device qualification and classification' v1.0, developed with NHS England
notes: Example 8: 'AVT agent ... analyses the transcript to autonomously determine necessary follow-up tests and place the relevant orders without clinician input or confirmation ... This AVT product, therefore, has a medical purpose and is a medical device.' Press release: 'AVT products intended to support diagnosis, treatment or prevention, or that take automated action such as placing orders without clinician review, are regulated as medical devices'. Example 3 (structured data into 'current medications lists, order sets' for a clinician to review, edit and confirm) is the rung-1 pattern. Rung 3 here means autonomous order-placing is a device-regulated path, not prohibited; prescription-only medicines would still need a reg. 214 'appropriate practitioner' prescription. NHS England's companion AVT guidance page did not load (bot wall).
short: MHRA: AI that places orders without review is a medical device

status_detail: non-binding international guidance
what_is_allowed: No prescribing rule. Principle that humans remain in control of medical decisions; full delegation of clinical judgement flagged as legally and ethically doubtful, though AI making well-defined decisions 'may be entirely justified' with compelling evidence. LMM guidance lists issuing a prescription as a higher-risk function needing a higher burden of proof, and expects LMMs to pre-emptively draft prescriptions (rung 1).
drug_scope: All clinical AI; prescriptions named as higher risk
liability_or_prescriber_of_record: Not specified
legal_basis: WHO, Ethics and governance of artificial intelligence for health (2021) s.6.5; WHO, Guidance on large multi-modal models (2025)
notes: LMM guidance: 'For those functions that are considered to be higher risk, such as providing a prescription or mental health advice to a person with severe depression ... the burden of proof will be higher'; also 'pre-emptive writing of automated prescriptions'. 2021: 'humans should remain in control of health-care systems and medical decisions'; s.6.5: 'there are signs of full delegation of routine medical functions to AI. Delegation of clinical judgement introduces concern about whether full delegation is legal'. Context only; not a ban.
short: WHO guidance on AI for health
